core_obligations: The two filtrations agree (proof lines 5100-5108): the quotient filtration of Y/X computed from the induced filtration on Y is F^pY/F^pX, and the induced filtration coming from the injection of Y/X into A/X is computed to be the same object, using that the filtration steps of subobjects are intersections with the filtration steps of A.
The remaining assertions (proof lines 5109-5110): the strictness of the six listed morphisms is proved in the same way as the first assertion.
proof_roadmap: Compute the quotient filtration on Y/X from the induced filtration on Y.
Compute the induced filtration on Y/X as a subobject of A/X.
Compare the two and repeat the computation for strictness.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that on the quotient of two subobjects of a filtered object the quotient filtration and the filtration induced from the ambient quotient agree, and that six specific morphisms between the objects involved are strict (statement lines 5085-5098). The proof is a complete argument for the first assertion: the quotient filtration is computed as F^pY/F^pX and the induced filtration from the injection into the ambient quotient is computed to be the same, using the description of the filtration steps of subobjects as intersections (proof lines 5100-5108); the strictness assertions are then said to be proved in the same way (proof lines 5109-5110). The non-formal content is the two computations of the filtration steps. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
